chapter_title: Concerning these Names: God, Rich One, and Angel; who they are.
chapter_note: The chapter is largely a systematic three-tier emanation teaching (god → rich one → angel) iterated across three contexts (land of light archetypes; emanations in the contest/worlds; then three ‘households’). The main late material is the dialogue/frame apparatus (“Once again…”, “His disciples asked…”, “The apostle speaks…”). Paragraph 9 uses “apostolate/embassy” language that likely reflects Mani’s self-presentation and mission vocabulary; despite cosmological content it reads as a later overlay into the teaching sequence rather than the oldest impersonal explication.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic opening with ‘Once again the enlightener speaks’ and rhetorical catechetical questions; functions as hagiographic container for the teaching.
Pure disciple-question frame (‘Tell us, our master’), no cosmological exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: There are these three archetypes [in the land of light, and there is no measure to] them!
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue attribution ‘The apostle speaks to them:’ (compilation frame marker; ‘apostle’ belongs to the later Kephalaia apparatus).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Underlying sentence is impersonal, structural (‘three archetypes… land of light… no measure’), but introduced by a clear dialogue-frame attribution.

paragraphs.core_text: So, the ones who are called 'god', are the gods whom the Father has summoned from himself. He has established them after the likeness of his greatness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal emanation logic (Father summons from himself; likeness of greatness) defining a named tier; no citation or institutional exhortation.

paragraphs.core_text: Conversely, these who are named 'rich [ ... ]', are the evocations of the first rich gods of the Father; because, when the Father had summoned (the first), they themselves summoned evocations. They called them 'rich'.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second tier defined by generative cascade (evocations of evocations) in a schematic ‘conversely’ style; fits core systematic taxonomy.

paragraphs.core_text: They too, the rich ones, have summoned their evocations. They call them 'angel'. These are the three archetypes who occur in the land of light. There is no measure to apply to them!
paragraphs.temporal_note: Completes the three-step structure (god → rich → angel) and closes with land-of-light measurelessness; strongly core, expository voice.

paragraphs.core_text: Once again, listen! Other persons who are named 'god' are the emanations who have come from the Father; the evocations of the Father whom he summoned forth. They came out to the contest and humiliated the enmity.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Still systematic definition, now second iteration (‘other persons…’) applying the category to cosmic struggle (‘contest’, ‘enmity’). The attention-getter ‘Once again, listen!’ is not the Kephalaia dialogue frame and reads as internal rhetorical stitching within the teaching.

paragraphs.core_text: Conversely, the 'rich ones' are the evocations of these first living words. They too, the rich ones, have come and performed and fulfilled the pleasure of the greatness, in the worlds that are above and below.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Parallel second-tier definition in the same schematic ‘conversely’ pattern; cosmological scope (‘worlds above and below’) without institutional markers.

Mission-language (‘embassy’, ‘apostolate’) and soteriological address to souls in the ‘building’ reads like Mani/community self-description grafted onto the third tier. Even without explicit NT citation, the register resembles later Christianized/Manichaean apostolic overlay rather than the oldest impersonal taxonomy.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, they are called 'god', all the gods who belong to the household of the Great Spirit.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed frame formula ‘Once again the enlightener speaks:’ (hagiographic compilation wrapper).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Underlying line continues the systematic triadic application (now to ‘households’), but the paragraph is introduced by a standard Kephalaia frame tag.

paragraphs.core_text: Conversely, the ones who are called 'angel', are all the angels who belong to the household of the Beloved of the Lights.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Schematic category-application (‘conversely… called angel… household of…’) using named cosmological entity; no frame/citation.

paragraphs.core_text: The ones who are called 'rich', are all the rich ones who belong to the household of the glorious Ambassador.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Completes the final triadic mapping to cosmological ‘households’ with a named being (Ambassador); impersonal taxonomic closure typical of core teaching.
